headline_for_review: C1 SETTLES IT: THE DEEP TAIL IS POISSON. phi = 0.895 +/- 0.154 (n=43, -0.58 sd) and 1.062 +/- 0.166 (n=50, +0.36 sd), every window within 1.6 sd of 1.0 with alternating signs, all bins at expected count >= 10. The null is INFORMATIVE, not empty: a seeded phi_true = 1.5 control returns 1.459 +/- 0.237 and 1.521 +/- 0.247, so the test would have seen real over-dispersion. Two prior attempts disagreed in opposite directions; this one has a power control and they did not.
second_headline: BOTH RETIREMENT NUMBERS REPRODUCE INDEPENDENTLY. Effective dof 1.5454 and 1.5135 against the red team's 1.55 and 1.51, plus the white-noise 422/471 and the C>=1000 1.81/1.90 -- all six agree on two independent implementations. The attenuation identity reproduces exactly on every structural quantity: 209.12591, 247.86603, 1147.23x, 948.73x, and a perfect model reading 0.7701x against their 0.769x.
coordinator_notes_for_review: THE PLUG-IN CONTROL IS THE QUIET RESULT. Running the plug-in lambda = C_T construction returns phi = 0.000 IDENTICALLY, because its leverage is exactly 1 and its residual is exactly 0. That is not a small methodological quibble: it means the construction the earlier attempts leaned on cannot produce a dispersion reading at all, in either direction.

A CONVENTION SENSITIVITY THAT WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY REPORTED, and it partly qualifies the record I wrote. The whole-band dof spans 1.51 to 2.35 across three defensible ways of combining the D-1 correlation with a per-row variance. The O(1)-not-O(n) conclusion -- which is what actually justifies retiring the statistic -- is robust across all three. The two-significant-figure '1.55' that DEC-20260803-52a750 quotes is not.

ANOM-7 BOUNDS AN EARLIER CLAIM. Four of the six rows in the '16-42 percent below the deep-tail floor' table are NOT reconstructible from BATCH-012's archived summaries -- different p, different s, or normalisation shifts of 0.1 to 0.83 bits. The executor flagged each reconstruction_valid: false and reported no unsupported number. The fix is concrete and cheap: archive residuals[T] per model per fit.

ANOM-4 IS A DISCLOSED WRONG PREDICTION. The executor predicted greedy observed-count binning would bias phi DOWN; it measured UP (0.927 against 0.895; 1.220 against 1.062), an effect comparable to one sd. Recorded rather than quietly dropped, which is what makes the binning rule visible as a live analysis choice at this resolution.
open_for_review: Does phi reproduce under a different windowing and a different rate estimator? ANOM-4 shows the binning rule moves it by about one sd.

The C < 10 rows carry NINE pooled increment events per file and admit no dispersion statistic at all -- and they are the rows the whole-band floor weights most heavily. Is that consistent with the attenuation identity's account?

ANOM-5: the two archived files DISAGREE about mid-band dispersion, 0.802 +/- 0.084 (-2.3 sd) against 1.106 +/- 0.067 (+1.9 sd), stable across every polynomial degree. Unexplained by the producer and deliberately not interpreted.
ANOM-3: one terminal wide bin reaches leverage 0.80, destabilising the analytic sd. Is the Monte-Carlo sd the right one to read throughout?
